cards.issue_title: CIBIL score is one required exact number
summary_4_lines: On Explore banks, CIBIL is a single required box (it shows 780).
People often do not know their exact score, only a band like 680–700.
They treated that exact box as the wrong control: they want a dropdown and/or a min–max range.
Minimum should be required; maximum optional. If someone puts a hoped-for higher score, the bank table can go empty.
cards.pinpoint: On Explore banks, the required CIBIL score field is a single exact number (780 on screen); they said users do not know an exact CIBIL and the field must be a selectable dropdown and/or a min–max range, with minimum compulsory and maximum optional.
cards.on_screen_object: Loan inputs CIBIL score* textbox #hlc-cibil (placeholder 780, required)
quotes_sample: Should I give him a drop down?
You don't need to know your exact Sibyl score.
Then the table will be empty.
related_discussion_one_liners: Amazon typeahead analogy from wb-rec-260815-2125 (cracked Amazon links; type 7 → next 5 scores; football 24 inches) — not a separate Amazon-link bug.
Font weight: typed amount normal; the type you are going to type extra weight — related to Amazon-style typeahead for CIBIL, not a second page object.
Aside: “You have to pay so much for a PM” — not a site issue.
Rejection psychology: if they think “my rejection is more,” they raise the minimum (e.g. 760); only-max 760 vs also-max showing max 760 — “This is what I like.”
User-future talk: 3/6 months, raise score 20 points, “show me what is possible” vs “I can’t increase it”; bounding the range (ASR max of 5 / 25); end “I want 2 rates. I want 2 loans.” is issue-02.
cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is the Loan inputs CIBIL score* box (#hlc-cibil) as a single exact number vs dropdown/min–max; issue-02 is the Overview Rate column showing one rate for a bank CIBIL band.

cards.issue_title: Bank table shows only one rate for a CIBIL band
summary_4_lines: On Explore banks, each bank row has a single Rate.
They said the bank actually gives a band such as 775 to 780, so one rate cannot be filtered or explained.
They asked which rate is the lowest, and on what basis.
At the end they said they want two rates and two loans, after opening Other charges and switching Prepayment to Balance transfer.
cards.pinpoint: On Explore banks Overview, each bank is shown with only one Rate, while they said the bank tells a CIBIL band such as 775–780, so they cannot filter or tell the user which rate applies; they asked which is the lowest rate and on what basis, and later said they want two rates and two loans.
cards.on_screen_object: Bank options Overview table Rate column (sortable header Rate)
quotes_sample: But we have to show him only one rate.
related_discussion_one_liners: Sits on top of issue-01 CIBIL min/max/dropdown; rejection, 680–700, 20 points, 6-month loan analogies belong with the input, not this Rate column.
“Maximum limit of 5” vs “25”: ASR disagrees; both about bounding a CIBIL range so a rate filter can work — not a separate issue.

Other charges / Prepayment method / Balance transfer: they switched Self funds → Balance transfer; some banks’ prepayment did change (Canara Nil→2%, BoB Nil→0.50%); they said BT will not change, then “No, no. I want 2 rates” — a check, not a separate BT-charges-wrong issue.
“Repayment charge and self-fund will be 300”: ASR; on screen Self funds prepayment is 2.00% / Nil, not “300.”
cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is the Overview Rate column showing one number per bank for a 775–780 CIBIL band (and “2 rates / 2 loans”); issue-01 is how the user enters CIBIL on the Loan inputs field.
